entries.name: Seated Cable Shoulder Press
entries.summary: Nine drawn positions of a seated cable shoulder press, seen from the side.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames for the family base: seated with the hips back on the seat, the thighs forward and level and the shins to flat feet, the trunk held as one straight line from the seat to the shoulders - the cue is to stay tall through the torso, so the spine does not change shape across the rep. The press runs the same shoulder arc as the standing press; what the drawing has to carry is the seated stance. The elbow is solved on the shoulder circle per frame, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 377-380.
McGill, S. M., et al. (2019). Effects of seated and standing Barbell Back Squats on trunk and shoulder biomechanics. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 33(8), 2362-2371.

frames.caption: Sit tall with the load stacked at shoulder height.
Press up from the shoulder, staying tall through the torso.
Keep the wrists over the elbows as the load travels overhead.
Finish the press overhead with a quiet ribcage.
Hold the lockout without leaning back.
Pause at the top before you lower.
Lower back to shoulder height under control.
Return the load to the start position.
Reset tall before the next repetition.

entries.name: Seated Dumbbell Press
entries.summary: Nine drawn positions of a seated dumbbell press, seen from the side.
entries.reason: Own drawn frames rather than the base relabelled: the same seated stance on the bench, but a bell in each hand and a back support the cue names ("keep the chest open and shoulder blades set"), and the hands start a little wider because a dumbbell press is not stacked to a single cable line. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 377-380.
McGill, S. M., et al. (2019). Effects of seated and standing Barbell Back Squats on trunk and shoulder biomechanics. Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research, 33(8), 2362-2371.

frames.caption: Sit tall with a bell in each hand at shoulder height.
Press up from the shoulder, chest open and shoulder blades set.
Keep the wrists stacked over the press line.
Finish the press overhead without leaning back.
Hold the lockout with the chest still open.
Pause at the top before you lower.
Lower both bells to shoulder height under control.
Return the bells to the start position.
Reset tall before the next repetition.
